claim: The one-line subject of the mechanism that gives each run its own checkout of one repository.
query: git worktree manage multiple working trees attached same repository
snippet: Manage multiple working trees attached to the same repository.
title: Git - git-worktree Documentation

claim: Multiple simultaneous checkouts of one repository, which is what lets concurrent runs work without cloning per run.
query: git repository multiple working trees check out more than one branch at a time worktree
snippet:
A git repository can support multiple working trees, allowing you to check
out more than one branch at a time. With git worktree add a new working
tree is associated with the repository, along with additional metadata
that differentiates that working tree from others in the same repository.
The working tree, along with this metadata, is called a "worktree".
title: Git - git-worktree Documentation
topic: Why more than one checkout exists

claim: The value domain: exactly one main worktree unless the repository is bare, and any number of linked ones.
query: git linked worktree main worktree git-init git-clone one main zero or more linked
snippet:
This new worktree is called a "linked worktree" as opposed to the "main
worktree" prepared by git-init[1] or git-clone[1].
A repository has one main worktree (if it’s not a bare repository) and
zero or more linked worktrees. When you are done with a linked worktree,
remove it with git worktree remove.
title: Git - git-worktree Documentation
topic: The two kinds of checkout and how many of each

claim: Eight subcommands, named by the documentation's own synopsis - the operation set at this card.
query: git worktree add list lock move prune remove repair unlock synopsis
snippet:
git worktree add [-f] [--detach] [--checkout] [--lock [--reason <string>]]
[--orphan] [(-b | -B) <new-branch>] <path> [<commit-ish>]
git worktree list [-v | --porcelain [-z]]
git worktree lock [--reason <string>] <worktree>
git worktree move <worktree> <new-path>
git worktree prune [-n] [-v] [--expire <expire>]
git worktree remove [-f] <worktree>
git worktree repair [<path>…​]
git worktree unlock <worktree>
title: Git - git-worktree Documentation

claim: The first typed refusal: one branch cannot be checked out by two worktrees at once, and the override has two levels.
query: git worktree add refuses branch already checked out another worktree force twice locked
snippet:
By default, add refuses to create a new worktree when
<commit-ish> is a branch name and is already checked out by
another worktree, or if <path> is already assigned to some
worktree but is missing (for instance, if <path> was deleted
manually). This option overrides these safeguards. To add a missing but
locked worktree path, specify --force twice.
title: Git - git-worktree Documentation
topic: What add refuses, and what overrides it

claim: The second refusal, with the same two-level override semantics.
query: git worktree move refuses locked worktree force specified twice destination assigned
snippet:
move refuses to move a locked worktree unless --force is specified
twice. If the destination is already assigned to some other worktree but is
missing (for instance, if <new-path> was deleted manually), then --force
allows the move to proceed; use --force twice if the destination is locked.
title: Git - git-worktree Documentation

claim: The third refusal: uncommitted work is protected, and a lock needs a stronger override than dirt does.
query: git worktree remove refuses unclean worktree force locked twice
snippet:
remove refuses to remove an unclean worktree unless --force is used.
To remove a locked worktree, specify --force twice.
title: Git - git-worktree Documentation

claim: The fourth refusal, and the one case where the override is a different flag rather than a repeated one.
query: git worktree -b refuses create new branch already exists -B overrides resetting
snippet:
By default, -b refuses to create a new branch if it already
exists. -B overrides this safeguard, resetting <new-branch> to
<commit-ish>.
title: Git - git-worktree Documentation

claim: The CI half of the card: the gate is declared in a file inside the repository it gates.
query: GitLab CI/CD pipelines fundamental component configured gitlab-ci.yml YAML keywords
snippet:
CI/CD pipelines are the fundamental component of GitLab CI/CD. Pipelines are configured
in a .gitlab-ci.yml file by using YAML keywords.
title: CI/CD pipelines | GitLab Docs
topic: What the gate is and where it is declared

claim: The gate's entry points, which are the same four doors this repo's own examples use - push, merge request, schedule, manual.
query: GitLab pipelines run automatically events pushing branch merge request schedule manually
snippet:
Pipelines can run automatically for specific events, like when pushing to a branch,
creating a merge request, or on a schedule. When needed, you can also run pipelines manually.
title: CI/CD pipelines | GitLab Docs

claim: Stages are sequential and jobs within one are parallel, and a failing stage stops the pipeline - the ordering and the failure rule together.
query: GitLab stages group jobs run in sequence parallel all jobs succeed moves next stage fails ends early
snippet:
Stages, which define how to group jobs together. Stages run in sequence, while the jobs
in a stage run in parallel. For example, an early stage could have jobs that lint and compile
code, while later stages could have jobs that test and deploy code. If all jobs in a stage succeed,
the pipeline moves on to the next stage. If any job in a stage fails, the next stage
is not (usually) executed and the pipeline ends early.
title: CI/CD pipelines | GitLab Docs
topic: The gate's ordering and failure semantics
